title: Robeco expands Australian equities offering for super
full_text:
Superannuation funds facing pressure over benchmark-relative investment outcomes are among the investors targeted by Robeco’s new Australian equities Enhanced Indexing strategy.
The launch comes as the Your Future, Your Super performance test has sharpened funds’ focus on benchmark-relative outcomes, increasing pressure on core allocations to perform consistently, according to Robeco.
The manager is positioning the strategy between passive exposure and high-conviction active management, aiming to generate additional returns while controlling the risk of departing from the benchmark.
Robeco said Australia’s market-capitalisation-weighted benchmark was heavily concentrated in a small number of large banks and miners. While active managers could pursue additional returns, large stock or sector positions could introduce more benchmark-relative risk than institutions wanted in a core allocation.
The strategy is benchmarked against the S&P/ASX 300 Index and is expected to hold around 150 positions across the investment universe.
Wilma de Groot, Robeco’s head of core quant equity and head of quant portfolio management, who has portfolio oversight of the strategy, said the approach addressed the Australian market’s concentration.
“While Australia is a concentrated market, it is broad and liquid enough to support a diversified systematic approach – where quantitative stock selection combined with disciplined risk control offers an alternative to relying on passive exposure alone,” de Groot said.
“We’re giving investors a way to stay close to a benchmark while managing a concentration problem that passive exposure alone doesn’t solve.”
Tracking error is managed through Robeco’s in-house risk model, which assesses sector, style, macro and statistical exposures together.
The strategy is available through a mandate rather than a pooled fund, allowing investors to define risk budgets, exclusions, sustainability preferences and implementation requirements at the outset.
Robeco’s head of Australia and New Zealand, Stephen Dennis, said the launch responded to demand from local institutions.
“Australian institutional investors have been telling us they want a core equity solution that can navigate the concentration of the local market without taking on the swings that come with high-conviction active management,” Dennis said.
“Bringing our globally established Enhanced Indexing capability to Australian equities is a direct response to that. It gives superannuation funds and other institutions a research-led option that stays close to the benchmark, manages risk deliberately, and can be tailored to their own requirements.”
Robeco’s quantitative portfolio management team leads day-to-day management, supported by Hong Kong-based head of APAC fundamental Joshua Crabb and Sydney-based client portfolio manager Michael Lin.
The firm has operated in Australia since 2012 and has approximately $60 billion in assets under management locally.
